title: The team's patterns as experiments: a second opinion on the family, and a debate between two designers
request: Phase 6 (the owner): finish the multi-agent team in the agreed order; 28.6 measures two patterns, each kept only where it beats the single agent on its own field, with a gate fixed before the run and a budget of about two euros a pattern.
spec: docs/guides/PHASE6_MULTI_AGENT_PLAN.md, package 28.6 and D5 (patterns the team may use, each measured before kept)
plan: Choose the material: the dev people and the spent fifth sealed set read as dev material, its failures read while designing, so a result is dev evidence only.
Build the second opinion: two readers of the family, a judge that asks the person only where they differ, the choice read by code.
Build the debate: the solution planner and a challenger, a judge on disputes, every kept change through the planner's checks.
Fix each pattern's gate in code before any run, with a runner that stores only a whole, clean run and a switch on only where the result passed.
Have the change reviewed twice before spending, then run both and store their results.

decisions.decision: The second opinion lives in the Home agent, used by both the loop and the walk, and acts only where the reader's family and the rules' family disagree.
decisions.why: Measured against the single agent with nothing else changed; agreement or a single reading asks nothing, so the person's time is spent only where two readings conflict.

decisions.decision: The person's choice is read by hand-written cue phrases of each family, never by a model and never from words taken from a family's meaning.
decisions.why: The first reading chose from words such as not, review or predict; a choice must be the person's, and an ambiguous answer keeps the card.

decisions.decision: One reader serves both arms of the second opinion with its answers remembered.
decisions.why: Two readers answer identical prompts differently, and that noise could decide a gate measured on one or two people.

decisions.decision: The debate's challenger and judge run on the cheap tier (Haiku), the planner on the standard tier, its answer shared by both arms.
decisions.why: On Sonnet a debate costs about twice a single designer and could never meet the gate's 1.5 times bound; sharing the planner's answer makes the debate the only difference.

decisions.decision: The debate runs although it is expected to fail on this material.
decisions.why: No baseline holdout failure here is one a designer may fix, and the run is cheap; it is run for the record and to capture the designers' proposals, with the expectation written before the run.

change: dclab_core/second_opinion.py (Opinion v1, judge_family, read_choice), dclab_core/debate.py (Debate v1, the challenger and the judge), their prompts, dclab_core/plan.py (column-list entries shaped as the rules write them), dclab-core 0.81.0; dclab_rnd/draft/chat.py (the judge's question, the choice, the served path), draft/coordinator.py (a decline), draft/work.py (the switch), ledger/capture.py, orchestra/patterns.py and settings.py, models/settings.py (two purposes), agent_eval/journeys (the gates, the runner, the designers at the save); tests/test_second_opinion.py, tests/test_debate.py.

findings.defect: A debate on Sonnet could never pass its cost bound.
findings.scenario: Two designers and a judge on the standard tier cost about twice a single designer, against a bound of 1.5 times.
findings.cause: The seats' tier was not chosen with the bound in mind.
findings.fix: The challenger and the judge run on the cheap tier, the planner's answer is shared by both arms.

findings.defect: The challenger's request was refused before it was sent.
findings.scenario: A first design that kept a column out nested a list of objects in the evidence, which the evidence check refuses as a table.
findings.cause: Choices were sent as they are, not as the compact text the rules' plan uses.
findings.fix: Every designer's choice reaches a model as compact text.

findings.defect: The designers could not read a project whose outcome comes from a file of known cases.
findings.scenario: On the delivery fraud journeys the outcome is joined from the labels, so the table alone had no outcome column.
findings.cause: The table was read without the engine's label join.
findings.fix: The labels are joined as the engine joins them before the designers read the data.

findings.defect: Importing the problem card in a fresh interpreter failed.
findings.scenario: The main product's first import of the card raised a circular import, and the walk's tests errored.
findings.cause: The new modules imported the card and the planner at load time while the contracts imported them back.
findings.fix: Both read the card and the planner only when used; a test imports each module first in a fresh interpreter.

findings.defect: The team settings route's test failed on the new keys.
findings.scenario: The route returned two switches the test did not expect.
findings.cause: The test pinned the old keys.
findings.fix: The test expects the switches and that turning one on is refused while nothing passed.

findings.defect: A run on a few people could be stored as a pass.
findings.scenario: A run on one person gained one card and was stored, turning the switch on.
findings.cause: The runner stored whatever subset it ran.
findings.fix: A subset is never stored.

findings.defect: A broken baseline journey counted for the pattern.
findings.scenario: One baseline journey raised, scored nothing, and the arm looked strictly better.
findings.cause: Broken journeys were not counted.
findings.fix: A broken journey in either arm refuses the pass and the store.

findings.defect: The pattern's arm ran outside the private scope the baseline had.
findings.scenario: Any other model purpose would have been live in the arm and not in the baseline.
findings.cause: The scope listed only the reader and the critic.
findings.fix: The patterns' keys run under the same scope.

findings.defect: The gate's rule on asking twice was looser than the plan's.
findings.scenario: A family asked at a chat stop and again by the judge was not counted.
findings.cause: The count compared tags, not fields, and allowed as many as the baseline.
findings.fix: Nobody may be asked a field twice, counted on the field.

findings.defect: A card gained by the reader's noise could pass the gate.
findings.scenario: The arm won a card where the judge never asked.
findings.cause: Every gain counted.
findings.fix: Only gains where the judge asked and the person chose count, against every loss.

findings.defect: A shape answer was taken as the person's choice.
findings.scenario: An answer saying a yes or no for each order flipped a rare event card to a class.
findings.cause: The rules' shape reading counted as a choice.
findings.fix: A shape never chooses; only a named choice, one family's cue or a stated reading does.

findings.defect: The judge asked over a kind the person stated.
findings.scenario: A person who chose time to event on the Solution page was asked again.
findings.cause: The stated kind was left in the rules' reading.
findings.fix: No question when the person stated the kind.

findings.defect: With a model serving Home the person's choice was never read.
findings.scenario: The model made a tool step, so its turn never reached the answer, and the question stayed open.
findings.cause: Only the script's turn read answers.
findings.fix: A pending second opinion is read by code before the model's turn.

findings.defect: Choices were recomputed when the answer arrived.
findings.scenario: A click on an option shown before the draft changed could be declined.
findings.cause: The verdict was not kept with the question.
findings.fix: The verdict travels with the question and the shown options are read.

findings.defect: The result named no model, and an unpriced run met the cost bound.
findings.scenario: Both arms spent nothing when usage had no price, and the cost check passed.
findings.cause: The models came from a missing attribute; the bound did not need a priced baseline.
findings.fix: The result keeps each seat's report; the bound needs a priced baseline.

findings.defect: The capture map named only the build's family decision.
findings.scenario: The judge's family decision was written without its place in the map.
findings.cause: The map was not updated.
findings.fix: The map names both writers.

findings.defect: The debate cannot pass its gate on this material.
findings.scenario: Of the baseline's holdout failures one is already the rules' plan and two need a kept-out column back, which no designer may do.
findings.cause: The material holds no failure a designer may fix.
findings.fix: The expectation is written before the run; the run is for the record and the capture; the switch stays off.

findings.defect: Answers the planner's checks accepted broke the solution built from the plan.
findings.scenario: A column to confirm given as a name, or an identifier given as an object, raised when the solution was made.
findings.cause: The guard checked only that a column list was a list.
findings.fix: Each entry must have the shape the rules write: names for identifiers, column and reason, column and question.

findings.defect: A designer's kept-out column already in the proposal refused the solution.
findings.scenario: On a churn journey a designer kept out a column the proposal already kept out, and the save failed.
findings.cause: The design's additions were filtered against the rules' plan, not the proposal.
findings.fix: A column already kept out is not added again.

findings.defect: The challenger's silence was read as a dispute.
findings.scenario: Every change of the planner went to the judge, who could drop one the challenger accepted.
findings.cause: Only changes both restated counted as agreed.
findings.fix: A first-design change the challenger left alone is agreed; a dispute is where it chose otherwise.

findings.defect: Two independent readers made the second opinion's arms differ by noise.
findings.scenario: A single noise loss among 45 people would have failed the gate.
findings.cause: Each arm had its own reader.
findings.fix: One reader with remembered answers serves both arms.

findings.defect: Words taken from a family's meaning chose wrongly.
findings.scenario: Not sure chose uplift, review chose anomaly, predict chose segmentation.
findings.cause: The cues were the words of each family's description.
findings.fix: Hand-written cue phrases, negations and not sure read as no choice; no written person's answer picks a wrong family of any pair.

findings.defect: A decline recorded the rules' family although the reader's stood.
findings.scenario: A card that kept the reader's uplift was recorded as the rules' class.
findings.cause: The record took the rules' reading on a decline.
findings.fix: The family that stands is recorded, with the reader as its answerer when it is the reader's.

findings.defect: A question asked and never answered counted as the person's choice.
findings.scenario: A journey that left the judge's question open would have counted as the pattern's gain.
findings.cause: Asked and not declined was read as chosen.
findings.fix: A gain is the pattern's only where the person answered and the answer chose.

findings.defect: The debate's switch reached nothing in the product.
findings.scenario: Turning it on after a pass would have changed nothing.
findings.cause: No serving path reads it.
findings.fix: The switch refuses until a serving path reads it.

findings.defect: A declined family question did not stop the judge.
findings.scenario: In the walk, a family the critic sent back and the person declined would be asked again by the judge.
findings.cause: Only answered family questions blocked the judge.
findings.fix: Any earlier family question blocks it.

outcome: Both patterns are built and measured honestly: the second opinion asks only where two readings conflict and reads the choice by code, the debate checks every change as the planner's, and each switch turns on only where a whole, clean run passed its gate.
lessons: A gate must count only what the pattern did: a gain the pattern did not make is noise, and a loss anywhere counts.
Check a gate's bounds against the arm's cost before choosing the models: a debate on the strong tier could never pass.
Read a person's answer to a choice by what only one choice means, and let anything ambiguous keep what stands.
risks: The fifth sealed set's failures were read while designing: its results are dev evidence, and the sixth sealed set judges.
The cue phrases were checked on 45 written people; real people will say things they do not hold.
